label: Temperature Gauge
description: Thick progress arc with an outer tick scale and a large coloured value with unit.
howTo: Bind `series[0].data[0].value` and `series[1].data[0].value` to the same temperature tag (the second series is the thin darker rim).
Set `min` / `max` on both series to the engineering range; `splitNumber` controls how many numbered ticks appear.
Change the unit in `series[0].detail.formatter` (`{value} °C`). The two arc colours are `series[0].itemStyle.color` and `series[1].itemStyle.color`.
For a ready-made dial driven by simple props (value, min, max, unit), see the Dial Gauge component; use this option when you need full control.

label: Ring Gauge
description: Three concentric progress rings from one series with pill-shaped value labels in the centre.
howTo: Bind `series[0].data[0].value`, `data[1].value` and `data[2].value` to three percentages (0–100). Each data item draws one ring, from the outside in.

Rename the rings with `data[n].name`. Each item carries its own `title.offsetCenter` and `detail.offsetCenter`, which stack the captions in the centre: keep them when you bind, or bind only the `value` fields.
For a scale other than 0–100 set `series[0].min` / `max` and change `detail.formatter` (`{value}%`).
`axisLine.lineStyle.width` is the total band width shared by all rings; add a fourth data item and it is divided by four. `axisLine.lineStyle.color` is the neutral track behind the rings.

label: Stage Speed Gauge
description: Wide band in three coloured stages with ticks inside the band, a needle and a value with unit.
howTo: Bind `series[0].data[0].value` to the speed tag and `series[0].max` to the top of the range.

The stages are `series[0].axisLine.lineStyle.color`: a list of `[fraction, colour]` pairs where the fraction is the END of the stage as a share of the range (0.3 = 30 %). Bind it to move the limits at runtime.
The needle and the value take the colour of the stage they are in (`color: "auto"` / `"inherit"`). Change the unit in `detail.formatter`.

label: Grade Rating Gauge
description: Semicircle with a thin four-colour arc, pointer triangle, score and caption; grade names come from a hidden pie series.
howTo: Bind `series[0].data[0].value` to a score between `min` and `max` (0–100); `data[0].name` is the caption.
The band colours are `series[0].axisLine.lineStyle.color` as `[fraction, colour]` pairs.

The grade names are drawn by the second, invisible pie series (`series[1]`): one data item per band, left to right. Keep its `data` names, label colours and item count in sync with the bands; give an item a larger `value` if its band is wider.
ECharts can only label gauge ticks with a formatter function, which a JSON prop cannot hold; the hidden pie is the function-free way to get the same look.

label: Progress Gauge
description: Classic dial whose band fills up to the value, with a ringed hub and a large value underneath.
howTo: Bind `series[0].data[0].value` to the tag; set `min` / `max` for a range other than 0–100.
Change or remove the unit in `series[0].detail.formatter`.
The filled band and the needle use the first theme colour; set `series[0].itemStyle.color` to override it, or bind it for an alarm colour. The unfilled track is `axisLine.lineStyle.color`.

label: Speed Gauge
description: Half dial with a rounded glowing progress arc, tapered needle and a boxed value with a small unit.
howTo: Bind `series[0].data[0].value` to the speed tag and `series[0].max` to the top of the range (keep `splitNumber` a divisor of the range for round tick labels).
The value box uses rich text: `detail.formatter` is `{value|{value}}{unit|bpm}`; replace `bpm` with your unit and style the two parts under `detail.rich`.
Arc and needle colour: `series[0].itemStyle.color` (and `shadowColor` for the glow).

label: Multi Title Gauge
description: Three pointers on one dial, each with its own title and coloured value badge below.
howTo: Bind `series[0].data[0].value`, `data[1].value`, `data[2].value` to three tags that share one scale; each item draws its own pointer and progress arc.

Each data item positions its caption and value badge with `title.offsetCenter` / `detail.offsetCenter` (percent of the radius from the centre). Add a fourth item by spacing the x offsets, e.g. -60 %, -20 %, 20 %, 60 %.
The pointers take the theme colours in order; set `data[n].itemStyle.color` to fix one.

label: Barometer Gauge
description: Dual-scale dial: an outer scale in kPa and an inner scale in psi share one needle.
howTo: Bind `series[0].data[0].value` to the reading in the OUTER unit (kPa here). Only the first series has a needle.
The inner scale is a second gauge series with no pointer. It is not linked to the outer one: choose `series[1].max` so both scales describe the same range (700 kPa is about 100 psi).
Captions: `series[0].data[0].name` (measurement) and `series[1].data[0].name` (inner unit). The outer unit is in `series[0].detail.formatter`.
